q: The Wolfram classification of cellular automata (Classes I-IV) places Class IV CA near the 'edge of chaos'. Class IV CA are characterised by:
opts: Seemingly random behavior without simple global patterns
Complex, localised patterns with persistent structures (gliders)—potentially computationally universal
exp: Class IV CA (like Conway's Game of Life, Rule 110) exhibit complex localised structures that interact in complicated ways. They live at the 'edge of chaos' between simple (periodic/ordered) and fully chaotic behavior, and are candidates for (or proven to be) computationally universal.
